summary.headline: Bare or nearly bare for 4.5 months a year (Oct-May); 32% of the year's erosive rain lands on that exposed soil.

why.text: This is what the field does today. Every alternative is measured against it with the same models, so the comparison is like for like.
Where it holds up: save water and ride out drought; keep soil covered and in place; income, forage and markets.
Where the data shows strain: build organic matter and nitrogen.
Staying with it is a legitimate choice. It needs no new equipment, markets or learning, and its risks are ones you already know.

evidence.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)
evidence.statement: About 991 mm (39 in) of rain and snow a year
evidence.detail: Year-to-year swing is 20%. The wettest months are May, Jun, Aug. Annual total is falling 49 mm per decade (not statistically clear yet).

evidence.dataset: Station-interpolated daily weather (ground reference)
evidence.statement: Satellite rain reads 5% lower than the gauges here
evidence.detail: Gauges (Daymet) 1010 mm, GPM IMERG 964 mm, MERRA-2 838 mm a year. The fused estimate leans 82% on gauges.

evidence.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)
evidence.statement: 46% of the year's soil-moving rain falls in May, Jun, Aug
evidence.detail: 19 days a year bring more than 12.7 mm (half an inch). The biggest single day on record was 65 mm. Heaviest-day rainfall is rising 1.7 mm per decade (not statistically clear yet).

evidence.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)
evidence.statement: 6 days a year reach 35 C (95 F)
evidence.detail: The last eight years averaged 6 such days against 7 in the first eight. The count is flat over the record. Mean temperature is rising 0.43 C per decade (not statistically clear yet).

evidence.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)
evidence.statement: Frost-free season: about 174 days
evidence.detail: Typical last spring frost Apr 22 (one year in ten as late as May 2); first fall frost Oct 16 (one year in ten as early as Oct 5).

evidence.dataset: MERRA-2 meteorology + GPM IMERG precipitation (daily, point)
evidence.statement: The air can take up 1.0 times more water than falls as rain
evidence.detail: Reference evapotranspiration is 1013 mm a year against 991 mm of precipitation. In Jun-Aug demand exceeds rain by 97 mm.

evidence.dataset: Root-zone soil wetness GWETROOT, standing in for SMAP L4
evidence.statement: 1.9 notably dry root-zone months a year recently, 1.5 in the early 2000s
evidence.detail: A dry month is one where root-zone wetness sits more than one standard deviation below normal for that month. Driest years: 2006, 2012, 2023. Warm-season root-zone wetness is falling 0.009 units (0-1 scale) per decade (not statistically clear yet).

evidence.dataset: Regional terrestrial water storage trend (published mascon analyses)
evidence.statement: Regional water storage is holding or rising: +0.6 cm of water a year
evidence.detail: Upper Midwest / Corn Belt: wetter decades; storage is not the limiting factor. GRACE measures a ~300 km footprint, so this is the region, not your well.

evidence.dataset: MODIS Terra NDVI (MOD13Q1)
evidence.statement: From orbit the field looks bare or dormant in 7 months of the year
evidence.detail: MODIS greenness (NDVI) stays under 0.30 in Oct-Apr and peaks at 0.91 in Jul (2019-2023, 115 clear composites).

evidence.dataset: MODIS Terra daytime land-surface temperature (MOD11A2)
evidence.statement: The ground surface averages 35 C at mid-morning in Jun
evidence.detail: That is +7 C against the average daily high air temperature. A large gap is the signature of dry or bare soil: a well-watered canopy stays close to air temperature.

evidence.dataset: MODIS evapotranspiration, gap-filled (MOD16A2GF)
evidence.statement: Satellites estimate 615 mm a year actually evaporates from this pixel
evidence.detail: MODIS MOD16 actual ET is 62% of precipitation. Above 100% points to irrigation or shallow groundwater; MOD16 is known to under-read irrigated fields.

evidence.dataset: SSURGO via Soil Data Access (dominant component, 0-30 cm weighted)
evidence.statement: Nicollet loam, 5.3% organic matter
evidence.detail: Nicollet loam, 1 to 3 percent slopes. The root zone can hold about 315 mm (12.4 in) of plant-available water. pH 6.2, drainage: somewhat poorly drained.

evidence.dataset: SSURGO via Soil Data Access (dominant component, 0-30 cm weighted)
evidence.statement: Hydrologic group B: this soil takes rain in moderately well
evidence.detail: Erodibility (Kw) is 0.28, on a scale where 0.2 is resistant and 0.5 is very erodible. The soil survey sets tolerable loss at 5 tons per acre a year.

evidence.dataset: SRTM GL1 30 m elevation (3x3 window, Horn slope)
evidence.statement: Slope about 0.6% at 337 m elevation
evidence.detail: From SRTM 30 m elevation over a 180 m window (6 m of relief). The soil survey lists 2% as representative.

evidence.dataset: Cropland Data Layer (CropScape point query)
evidence.statement: What satellites saw growing here
evidence.detail: USDA Cropland Data Layer: 2018 soybeans, 2019 corn, 2020 soybeans, 2021 corn, 2022 soybeans, 2023 corn.

evidence.dataset: Crop calendar from NASA POWER growing degree days + RUSLE
evidence.statement: Bare or nearly bare for 4.5 months a year (Oct-May); 32% of the year's erosive rain lands on that exposed soil.
evidence.detail: Mean ground cover 48%; modelled soil loss 2.3 tons/acre a year, 0.5 times the tolerable rate.

evidence.dataset: Monthly FAO-56 soil-water balance on fused rainfall and SSURGO water-holding capacity
evidence.statement: Uses 810 mm of water a year; 56% of rain and irrigation goes through the crop
evidence.detail: Runoff 37 mm, deep drainage 147 mm, unmet crop demand 0%.

evidence.dataset: One-pool soil carbon balance driven by residue, roots, temperature and tillage
evidence.statement: Returns 4.0 t/ha of carbon a year; soil carbon trend -0.23 t/ha a year
evidence.detail: Living roots 5.0 months a year. Legume and cover-crop nitrogen credit 18 kg/ha a year.

evidence.dataset: 24 years of NASA POWER weather run through the rotation, every phase in every year
evidence.statement: Replaying 2001-2024 weather: $419/acre on average, $239 in a bad year
evidence.detail: Worst years: 2012, 2006, 2021. Weather alone moves net return by $129/acre (one standard deviation).

benefits.summary: This is the reference. Benefits of the alternatives are measured against it.

items.topic: Rainfall (MERRA-2, bias-corrected): one pixel is 97x the width of this field
items.detail: Native resolution 55 km. Fused with IMERG and gauges by inverse-variance weighting.
items.close_by: A rain gauge, soil-moisture probe or well record on the farm beats any pixel this size.

items.topic: Root-zone soil moisture (SMAP-class): a stand-in product was used
items.detail: SMAP L4 root-zone moisture (9 km) needs an Earthdata login. MERRA-2 wetness is the same kind of model-assimilated estimate at coarser resolution, so seasonal anomalies agree well but field-to-field differences are invisible.
items.close_by: Add a NASA Earthdata login to pull the native product, or check against a field sensor.

items.topic: Land-surface temperature (MODIS, ECOSTRESS stand-in): one pixel is 2x the width of this field
items.detail: Native resolution 1 km. 8-day daytime composites averaged to months.
items.close_by: A rain gauge, soil-moisture probe or well record on the farm beats any pixel this size.

items.topic: Water storage trend (GRACE / GRACE-FO): one pixel is 527x the width of this field
items.detail: Native resolution 300 km. Regional trend used as context only; never downscaled to the field.
items.close_by: A rain gauge, soil-moisture probe or well record on the farm beats any pixel this size.

items.topic: Satellite check of the assumed crop calendar: strong agreement
items.detail: The crop calendar assumed for the current rotation and MODIS greenness move together (r = 0.93). The satellite record supports the assumed planting and harvest timing.
items.close_by: Edit the baseline rotation and planting dates to match your records.

items.topic: Compaction and hardpans below the surface
items.detail: No satellite sees a plough pan. The model assumes roots can use the full soil-survey depth; a compacted layer would cut water storage and the benefit of deep-rooted crops.
items.close_by: Push a penetrometer or dig a pit in spring when the soil is moist.

items.topic: Soil life, nematodes and disease inoculum
items.detail: Nematode counts, disease carry-over and microbial activity are invisible from orbit. Pest scores use rotation rules of thumb, not what is in this soil.
items.close_by: Pull nematode and soil-health samples; review the field's disease history.

items.topic: Tile lines, drainage and irrigation hardware
items.detail: Tile spacing, outlet condition, well capacity and system uniformity are not in any public dataset. One on/off setting stands in for them.
items.close_by: Check tile maps, well test records and a recent irrigation uniformity test.

items.topic: Varieties, hybrids and maturity groups
items.detail: Each crop is a single mid-range type. Variety choice can move maturity by weeks and drought or disease tolerance by a lot.
items.close_by: Match maturity and disease packages to the planting windows shown, with your seed adviser.

items.topic: Contracts, basis, leases and programme rules
items.detail: Prices are multi-year averages. Forward contracts, local basis, landlord terms, crop insurance and conservation-programme payments can outweigh every number here.
items.close_by: Price each crop with your buyer, lender and insurance agent before committing acres.

items.topic: Variation inside the field
items.detail: Weather inputs are 10-55 km pixels and the soil is one dominant map-unit component. Knolls, draws, sandy streaks and saline spots are averaged away.
items.close_by: Overlay yield maps or walk the field; consider zoning the rotation.

gaps.statement: Scores are planning estimates from a monthly model. Treat a difference of fewer points than the uncertainty shown for that dimension as a tie, and treat every dollar figure as a ranking aid, not a budget.

risks.title: Soybean returns every 2 year(s)
risks.detail: Recommended gap is 3 years. Watch for soybean cyst nematode, sudden death syndrome, white mold and for herbicide-resistant weeds selected by repeating the same programme.

risks.title: Soil is bare 4 months a year
risks.detail: Bare months coincide with part of the erosive-rain season. Residue management alone can change this without changing crops.

risks.title: Known risks are still risks
risks.detail: The current rotation's familiarity hides its exposure to one or two markets and one or two pest complexes.

strategies.tagline: Keep the crops you know. Change what happens between them.

why.text: You ranked "keep soil covered and in place" highly, and this rotation scores +34 points on it against today (Rain that soaks in up from 96% to 100%).
You ranked "build organic matter and nitrogen" highly, and this rotation scores +47 points on it against today (Organic matter after 10 years up from -0.11 % points to 0.13 % points).
The field is bare 4.5 months a year now, and 46% of erosive rain falls in May-Jun, Aug. Cover crops (Cereal rye cover, Rye + vetch + radish mix) cut bare time to 0.0 months.
No-till leaves residue on the surface: soil loss changes from 2.3 to 0.1 tons/acre a year.

items.label: Total crop water use
items.meaning: Evaporation plus transpiration from the field.

items.label: Crop water stress
items.meaning: Share of crop water demand the soil and irrigation could not meet.

items.label: Organic matter after 10 years
items.meaning: Projected change in topsoil organic matter.

items.label: Purchased nitrogen
items.meaning: Fertiliser nitrogen needed after legume and cover-crop credits.

items.label: Nitrogen lost below roots
items.meaning: Residual nitrate carried down by drainage.

items.label: Rain that soaks in
items.meaning: Share of rainfall that enters the soil instead of running off.

items.label: Months with living roots
items.meaning: Months something is growing and feeding soil life.

items.label: Pest and disease break
items.meaning: Years between host crops, plant-family and planting-season diversity.

items.label: Net return
items.meaning: Revenue minus operating, nitrogen, irrigation and cover-crop costs. Land cost excluded.

items.label: Net return in a bad year (1 in 5)
items.meaning: Mean minus the swing from 2001-2024 weather replayed through the rotation and from price volatility.

items.label: Income swing (share of revenue)
items.meaning: Year-to-year standard deviation of net return divided by gross revenue. Lower is steadier.

benefits.summary: Improves: Organic matter after 10 years up from -0.11 % points to 0.13 % points; Purchased nitrogen down from 90 kg N/ha/yr to 81 kg N/ha/yr; Nitrogen lost below roots down from 23.7 kg N/ha/yr to 6.9 kg N/ha/yr. Costs: Net return down from $520/ac/yr to $488/ac/yr.

risks.title: Herbicide carryover into rye + vetch + radish mix
risks.detail: Residual herbicides used in soybean (atrazine, HPPD inhibitors, sulfonylureas, imidazolinones) can injure rye + vetch + radish mix for 10-36 months, longer in dry or high-pH soil. Check every label's rotation interval against your spray records.

risks.title: Cover-crop termination timing
risks.detail: A cover crop terminated late can tie up nitrogen and slow soil warming. Agree a termination date and method (herbicide, roller, tillage, winter-kill) and confirm it meets crop-insurance cover-crop rules for your county.

risks.title: Cereal rye ahead of corn
risks.detail: Rye can host seedling diseases and tie up nitrogen for corn. Terminate 10-14 days before planting and consider starter nitrogen.

risks.title: Soybean still returns sooner than recommended
risks.detail: Every 2 year(s) against a recommended 3. Scout for soybean cyst nematode, sudden death syndrome, white mold.

risks.title: Moving to no-till
risks.detail: This soil is poorly drained, so residue will keep it colder and wetter in spring; strip-till may fit better. Expect a 3-5 year transition: planter set-up for residue, nutrient stratification, and different weed pressure.

risks.title: Try it on part of the field first
risks.detail: A strip trial for two seasons tests the planting windows, equipment and markets with little at stake.

summary.statement: "Corn + Cereal rye → Soybean + Rye + vetch + radish mix" fits your priorities best (76/100). It is effectively tied with 1 other option(s): the difference is inside the model's uncertainty.
